symptom: `mxcli check --references` prints "Check passed!" (exit 0) and `mxcli exec` then fails (exit 1) on the same script, over the order things are created *in the script* — with earlier statements already written, because exec is not transactional. exec's own message is already right ("… is defined later in this script — move its create statement before this one")
cause: `validateProgram` calls `sc.collectDefinitions(prog)` over the **whole program up front**, so every name in the script is "defined" for every statement and a forward reference is indistinguishable from a backward one. `annotateForwardRef` computes the diagnosis, but only in `ExecuteProgram`, *after* a statement has failed. `exec`'s pre-flight runs the package-level `ValidateProgram` (the no-project tier) and not the reference tier, so it was no safety net either
file: `mdl/executor/validate_definition_order.go` (`ValidateScriptDefinitionOrder`, MDL-ORDER01), wired into `mdl/executor/validate_program.go` beside `ValidateScriptPageOrder`; tests `mdl/executor/validate_definition_order_test.go`; repros `mdl-examples/bug-tests/955-forward-definition-order{,.fail,-tolerated,-or-modify-not-flagged}.mdl`
insight: Put it in the **no-project tier**, not under `--references`: that is what makes `exec`'s pre-flight refuse the script too, which turns a half-applied project into "Nothing was written" — the actual harm, and the part a `check`-only fix leaves in place. **Do not flag every forward reference**: measure which ones the executor resolves eagerly, because several do not fail — an entity's `EXTENDS`, `CALL JAVA ACTION`, `RETRIEVE … FROM`, and `CREATE <entity>` in a body all execute correctly with the definition after them (measured on 11.6.6), and a blanket rule rejects working scripts. **Only a plain CREATE later is sound with no project** (the MDL-PAGE01 argument: a plain CREATE asserts the document is absent, so the earlier reference could not have resolved against the project either); a later `CREATE OR MODIFY` fails exec just the same but cannot be judged without `-p`, and is deliberately left as known residue. Key by **kind as well as name** — Mendix namespaces documents by type — and skip `at == i` or a recursive microflow call reports itself. A bare `Module.Name` written as a type lands in `EnumRef` whether it means an entity or an enumeration (the TypeEnumeration/TypeEntity ambiguity), so accept both kinds unless `ExplicitEnum`. **`exec` exit 0 is not proof a forward reference is safe** — describe the result and check the reference actually got wired before adding it to the tolerated list. Regression probe that matters: run `check` over all of `mdl-examples/` and expect **zero** new findings (it found exactly one, a fixture whose GRANT genuinely preceded its entity). Issue #955
